estimand.population: synthetic subjects with completed 21-day observation windows and observable channel-exposure histories
estimand.treatment_or_exposure: presence versus absence of one channel in the subject's pre-outcome channel-exposure vector
estimand.outcome: qualifying conversion within the 21-day observation horizon
estimand.intervention: set the focal channel exposure component to present while holding the other observed channel-exposure components fixed
estimand.comparison: set the focal channel exposure component to absent while holding the other observed channel-exposure components fixed
estimand.temporal_ordering: all exposure components used by the candidate occur before the qualifying outcome; post-outcome touches are excluded
estimand.treatment_regime: component-wise intervention on a static pre-outcome multi-channel exposure vector
estimand.aggregation_target: population-average change in conversion probability for each channel

hypothesis.statement: An interpretable treatment-effect estimator that adjusts for the observed co-exposure vector can reduce synthetic causal-recovery error caused by observable selection structure relative to descriptive Phase 1 attribution rules, but it may fail when selection is driven primarily by hidden latent intent, when positivity is weak, or when the outcome model requires unmodeled interactions or time-varying structure.
hypothesis.why_it_might_address_selection: Conditioning treatment assignment and outcome estimation on the other observed channel-exposure components can remove association explained by observable co-exposure patterns instead of assigning credit from path position alone.
required_assumptions: consistency of the declared component-wise intervention
conditional exchangeability after adjustment for the declared observable co-exposure vector
sufficient positivity for treated and untreated subjects within observed covariate patterns
the static 21-day exposure-vector representation is adequate for the target estimand
expected_failure_conditions: unobserved latent intent remains a material common cause of exposure and conversion after observable adjustment
important treatment interactions are not represented by the selected estimator
treatment effects vary over time in a way the static exposure-vector estimand cannot capture
extreme propensity scores or sparse support create unstable weighting
identity fragmentation or measurement loss materially corrupts the observable exposure vector
hypothesis.rejection_interpretation: Failure means this Candidate 1 hypothesis is rejected for version 1.0.0; it must not be tuned and resubmitted under the same version after sealed-holdout exposure.

required_observable_inputs: channel identity for each observed touchpoint
available_adjustment_covariates: binary presence indicators for the other observed channels in the same pre-outcome exposure vector

representability.heterogeneous_effects: only the population-average marginal effect is targeted; heterogeneous effect structure is not estimated

uncertainty_target.target: 95% interval for each channel's population-average incremental conversion-probability estimate
uncertainty_target.requirement: finite interval covering every returned channel estimate

holdout_limitation_disclosure: The holdout-family architecture is public because this is a public research repository. Instantiated holdout seeds, parameter values, treatment effects, latent-intent strengths, interactions, selection mechanisms, and corruption settings remain sealed from candidate development. This provides strong research-process separation but is not equivalent to a completely secret external benchmark.
